references.title: Texturing and Modeling: A Procedural Approach

filters.name: Displace Vertices Randomly
filters.shortDescription: Move every vertex by an independently generated random vector.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Adds an independent uniformly distributed displacement to each coordinate of every vertex. With maximum displacement $d$, each coordinate offset lies in $[-d,d]$. Set a nonzero random seed to obtain repeatable results.

parameters.label: Maximum coordinate displacement
parameters.help: Maximum absolute displacement applied independently to each coordinate.

parameters.label: Recompute normals
parameters.help: Recompute face and vertex normals after displacement.

parameters.label: Random seed
parameters.help: Zero draws a fresh seed on every run, so repeated applications differ; any other value makes the displacement exactly reproducible.

filters.name: Displace Vertices by Fractal Brownian Motion
filters.shortDescription: Displace vertices along their normals using fractal Brownian motion.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Evaluates fractal Brownian motion (fBM) in normalized object space and displaces each vertex along a smoothed normal. The noise is the weighted sum $$N(\mathbf{x})=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} L^{-Hi}\,P(L^i\mathbf{x}),$$ where $P$ is VCGLib's three-dimensional Perlin noise, $n$ is the octave count, $L$ is lacunarity, and $H$ is the fractal increment. Lower $H$ retains more high-frequency detail.

parameters.label: Maximum height
parameters.help: Maximum positive displacement, relative to the mesh bounding-box diagonal.

parameters.label: Noise scale
parameters.help: Spatial size of the base noise features; smaller values produce finer detail.

parameters.label: Octaves
parameters.help: Number of Perlin-noise frequency bands.

parameters.label: Lacunarity
parameters.help: Frequency multiplier between consecutive octaves.

parameters.label: Fractal increment
parameters.help: Exponent controlling the spectral weight of higher frequencies.

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.help: Translation of the noise domain; changing it produces another morphology.

parameters.label: Normal smoothing steps
parameters.help: Laplacian smoothing iterations applied to normals before displacement.

filters.name: Displace Vertices by Standard Multifractal Noise
filters.shortDescription: Displace vertices using multiplicative standard multifractal noise.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Evaluates standard multifractal noise in normalized object space and displaces vertices along smoothed normals. Unlike additive fBM, its octave contributions are multiplied: $$N(\mathbf{x})=\prod_{i=0}^{n-1}\left(O+L^{-Hi}P(L^i\mathbf{x})\right).$$ The offset $O$ controls multifractality and the fractal increment $H$ controls the contribution of high frequencies.

parameters.label: Maximum height
parameters.help: Maximum positive displacement, relative to the mesh bounding-box diagonal.

parameters.label: Noise scale
parameters.help: Spatial size of the base noise features; smaller values produce finer detail.

parameters.label: Octaves
parameters.help: Number of Perlin-noise frequency bands.

parameters.label: Lacunarity
parameters.help: Frequency multiplier between consecutive octaves.

parameters.label: Fractal increment
parameters.help: Exponent controlling the spectral weight of higher frequencies.

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.help: Bias added to every octave before multiplication.

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.help: Translation of the noise domain; changing it produces another morphology.

parameters.label: Normal smoothing steps
parameters.help: Laplacian smoothing iterations applied to normals before displacement.

filters.name: Displace Vertices by Heterogeneous Multifractal Noise
filters.shortDescription: Displace vertices using elevation-dependent heterogeneous multifractal noise.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Evaluates a heterogeneous multifractal whose successive increments are modulated by the accumulated signal. This makes high-frequency detail depend on the local elevation already produced by lower octaves, yielding spatially varying roughness rather than a stationary noise field.

parameters.label: Fractal increment
parameters.help: Exponent controlling the spectral weight of higher frequencies.

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.help: Bias controlling the strength of multifractal modulation.

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.help: Translation of the noise domain; changing it produces another morphology.

parameters.label: Normal smoothing steps
parameters.help: Laplacian smoothing iterations applied to normals before displacement.

filters.name: Displace Vertices by Hybrid Multifractal Noise
filters.shortDescription: Displace vertices using signal-weighted hybrid multifractal noise.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Evaluates hybrid multifractal noise, where each octave controls how strongly the following octave contributes. The feedback is clamped to avoid unbounded amplification, producing terrain-like regions with locally varying roughness.

filters.name: Displace Vertices by Ridged Multifractal Noise
filters.shortDescription: Displace vertices using ridged multifractal noise.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Evaluates ridged multifractal noise by folding each Perlin signal around zero, subtracting it from the offset, and squaring it. Feedback controlled by the gain sharpens coherent ridges while suppressing detail away from them.

parameters.label: Maximum height
parameters.help: Maximum positive displacement, relative to the mesh bounding-box diagonal.

parameters.label: Noise scale
parameters.help: Spatial size of the base noise features; smaller values produce finer detail.

parameters.help: Frequency multiplier between consecutive octaves.

parameters.label: Fractal increment
parameters.help: Exponent controlling the spectral weight of higher frequencies.

parameters.label: Offset
parameters.help: Sets the ridge level before squaring the folded signal.

parameters.label: Gain
parameters.help: Controls feedback strength and ridge sharpness.

parameters.label: Seed
parameters.help: Translation of the noise domain; changing it produces another morphology.

parameters.help: Laplacian smoothing iterations applied to normals before displacement.
